title: Other frequent changing singular forms
summary: These words use a consonant stem before -ta/-tä: pieni (“small”) → pientä, suuri (“large”) → suurta, kieli (“language”) → kieltä, lapsi (“child”) → lasta, lohi (“salmon”) → lohta. Learn each stem; final -i alone does not predict it.
objectives: Form the singular partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.
Learn these five common consonant stems explicitly. Add -ta/-tä to pien-, suur-, kiel-, las- and loh-. These words do not follow one general rule for every word ending in i.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

commonMistakes: Learn the displayed stem of each word.
Do not add the ending to the unmodified dictionary word.
Keep pientä and lasta distinct from their plural forms.
